To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the ratios of string tensions in Z_4 lattice QCD are constant in the low-temperature region, and that this property extends to the entire confining phase.

(i) the ratios of k-strings tensions in the low-temperature region are constant up to terms proportional to T^3, (ii) the above ratios are actually constants in the whole confininig phase, (iii) the ratios of string tensions in Z_4 gauge theory can be obtained from the mass spectrum of the integrable spin model.

the ratios of string tensions in a three-dimensional lattice gauge theory are constant in the entire confining phase and equal to the corresponding ratios of the integrable spin chain model describing the infrared behavior of the gauge system at the deconfinement transition.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the behaviour of the string tension in the 3-D Z4 lattice gauge theory, and its relation to the behaviour of the mass gap of the 2-D spin chain.
the behaviour of ratios of string tensions in three-dimensional Z_2 and Z_4 lattice models.
the study of the infrared behaviour of gauge theories in the confining and the deconfinement phase.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, in the low-temperature confining region, the ratios of k-strings tensions in the 4-dimensional Z_N gauge theories with N even, are constant up to terms O(T^3) for all k, whereas, for N odd, the ratios of 2k-strings tensions are constant up to O(T^3), but the ratios of (2k+1)-strings tensions are not constant.
the string tensions in a three-dimensional gauge model are constant in the confining regime, up to corrections of order T^2, where T is the temperature.
the ratios of string tensions are constant up to corrections of order T^4 in the confining region of the gauge theory.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the string tension ratios of the three-dimensional Z_3 and Z_4 lattice models are constants in the whole confinement phase.
the string tensions of a gauge theory are not renormalized by quantum corrections.
we have found a way to obtain the ratio of string tension of a 3D gauge theory in the whole confinement phase by studying an integrable 2D model in the vicinity of a second-order phase transition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in three-dimensional gauge theories, the ratios of k-strings are constant up to terms that are exponentially small in the inverse coupling.
the ratios of string tensions are universal, in the sense that they are independent of the gauge group.
the string tension ratios in the 3d gauge system can be computed by studying the mass spectrum of the spin model.
